source.literal_observation: Fol. 1v has twelve wind busts: an outer Latin name band, an inner Greek alternate-name band, and one first-person spoke characterization per bust. Fol. 2r repeats twelve names with the corresponding sector characterizations and explicit relative relations such as left/right of another wind.

fixed_source_consequence: The historical constraint is a repeated twelve-record, multi-field correspondence with a fixed field order; it does not supply a Voynich word meaning or authorize a wind gloss.

target_endpoint.documented: The existing f67r2 crosswalk records a twelve-position lower sequence, including `okal` at f67r2.22, `okain.am` at .28, `opcholdy` at .31, and `ofar.oeoldan` at .34.
target_endpoint.missing: No already documented f67r2 partition supplies four co-owned fields (outer name, alternate name, profile, spoke) or a second complete target register. A fieldwise test is therefore unavailable without inventing target fields.

contrast.mechanism: One target record owns several parallel registers whose values co-vary in a fixed order.
contrast.rival: Four independent coordinate, attribute, and note lists happen to have twelve positions.
mechanism_consequences: A repeated target record should preserve linked field identity and constrained co-variation across its registers.
The same record schema should recur without assigning any field an English gloss.
rival_consequences: A change in one field need not be accompanied by a constrained change in the others.
Independent field permutations remain admissible even when the twelve positions align.

prior_difference: This is not the failed W73 shared-right action run (GDT929), which stopped on open `otey`/`chedy`, and not the older W73 wind-fingerprint/alignment route recorded by HIST:1ad444a70541438b. The proposed observable is field co-ownership, not wind names, cardinal orientation, rotation, or a guessed dictionary. The distinction remains prospective because the target fields are missing.
smallest_discriminator: Using only the existing twelve f67r2 positions, first document an author-visible multi-field partition; then require the same cross-field correspondence in repeated complete records. If no such partition is available, stop with no semantic inference.
assumption_costs: W.73's field grouping reflects a historical record convention rather than editorial packaging.
The f67r2 twelve positions are comparable to those records despite different topology.
Co-ownership can be observed without translated anchors.
strongest_likely_failure: The target has only a twelve-position layout, so apparent parallelism would be produced by arbitrary grouping; the W.73 homologue may be only a diagram-class resemblance.
decision: Source review only; no target test or meaning selected here. A new explicitly hypothetical field construction remains possible but was not supplied by this review.
